stories.title: Tech adoption is a cultural problem
stories.summary: Founders often blame pricing or onboarding when users refuse to abandon old habits for new tools. Daria, a sociology-trained consultant, argues that culture dictates adoption rather than innovation. The best tool in the room frequently loses to the one people already trust. Culture remains undefeated.

stories.title: Research adapts to AI speed
stories.summary: As AI agents automate code, software development economics shift from slow, deliberate setups to rapid, iterative cycles. Much like digital photography replaced film, the cost of each iteration has dropped. Learning now happens after the shot, because the shot itself has become nearly free.

stories.title: Journey mapping 101
stories.summary: A journey map visualizes the process a person follows to accomplish a goal. By compiling user actions into a timeline and layering on thoughts and emotions, designers create a narrative of the experience. It serves as a tool for refining how users interact with a system.

stories.title: The flawlessness of modern algorithms
stories.summary: Designers have spent years refining machines to be flawless. According to the UX Collective, this pursuit of perfection is now resulting in a sense of absence. The crooked plate is beginning to feel more human than the algorithm.

stories.title: AI as a design material
stories.summary: Creative makers have historically learned mediums by working directly with them, from grinding pigments to writing HTML. The field is now treating AI models as the next material. Learning requires building, though the industry continues to argue about the specifics.

stories.title: Product designers split on AI
stories.summary: Product design teams are approaching AI from fundamentally different perspectives, according to speakers at PUSH UX. Some teams cautiously experiment within established processes, while others have integrated AI to bridge research, prototyping, and code. The divide reflects how teams organize their work.

stories.title: Accessibility and AI readiness
stories.summary: Companies building accessible websites are inadvertently making them easier for AI to read and cite. With 49 percent of U.S. adults using AI chatbots and 58 percent of generative AI users delegating tasks, LLMs are becoming the primary interface for information retrieval.

stories.title: The rule of the disabled button
stories.summary: Eight major design systems, including Material and GOV.UK, maintain a disabled state for buttons. The practice, which prevents interaction until a field is populated, remains a standard component in modern design systems. Clicking a greyed-out button continues to yield no result.

stories.title: Below the surface
stories.summary: Oeps, je hebt JavaScript nodig voor deze website. The archaeological research project of the North/South metro line lends the River Amstel a voice in the historical portrayal of Amsterdam. The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: Building interfaces that understand intent
stories.summary: Most current software is deterministic, meaning the same action always produces the same result. Agustin Barrientos suggests that interfaces are evolving to move beyond this, aiming to understand what a user wants to do rather than forcing them to navigate static menus.

stories.title: The logic of industry shifts
stories.summary: For decades, professional success often relied on predicting the outcome of specific technological shifts, such as the rise of mobile or the transition to web apps. These predictions were rarely certain at the time. History suggests that if X happens, Y usually follows.

stories.title: New York bodega cats
stories.summary: Bodega Cats of New York documents the working cats of the city. The project highlights the efforts to legalize these animals, which keep shops rodent-free. The book and its associated media coverage explore the intersection of urban retail and feline labor.

stories.title: Retro UI design for AI agents
stories.summary: Viacheslav Sheikin designed the Ardor Retro Computer interface to stage a cloud AI agent on a 8-color phosphor CRT. The design replaces standard SaaS pricing grids with scanlined visuals and keyboard-first controls. It prioritizes a specific aesthetic over contemporary web conventions.

stories.title: Porto Rocha rebrands Almeida & Dale
stories.summary: Porto Rocha built the new brand identity for gallery Almeida & Dale using a custom typeface and a single strong blue. The color serves as the foundation for the entire system, including catalogues and fair posters. The work prioritizes the artwork over the gallery's scale.

stories.title: Nubank brand refresh by Koto
stories.summary: Koto updated the Nubank brand to support a customer base of 140 million. The refresh introduced proprietary typefaces and a modular system of layers and colors. The bank aims to maintain a flexible identity that scales across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia.

stories.title: Blæst visual identity by Kurppa Hosk
stories.summary: Stockholm studio Kurppa Hosk designed the identity for rainwear label Blæst around the concept of natural disruption. The branding features a vortex mark and blown grotesque type, intended to pit Nordic weather against city tailoring. The tension is stitched into the neck labels.

stories.title: Alpha Bank retail transformation
stories.summary: Alpha Bank is updating its 147-year-old retail branches to move away from the traditional administrative waiting room aesthetic. The project, led by Pentagram and Dalziel & Pow, aims to modernize the banking experience beyond simply applying a new coat of paint.

stories.title: Anagram brand identity by Pact
stories.summary: Pact designed the Anagram identity as a kaleidoscopic system that never settles into a fixed shape. The firm, which backs decentralized networks, requested an identity that avoids the aesthetics of cold finance or speculative hype. The resulting system uses 8-bit color and shifting grids.

stories.title: A book cover that doubles as a table of contents
stories.summary: Designer Ibán Ramón has published Escenas del diseño valenciano Vol. 2 with a recessed summary sheet glued to its cloth cover. The table of contents is printed directly onto the front board. The design removes the need for a dust jacket, which the publisher notes can be torn or tossed.

stories.title: Tactile packaging for a soap atelier
stories.summary: Twice Shy has redesigned the packaging for Tula Louise, a London soap brand. The new look uses vellum wraps and metal clips to distinguish the products from standard bath-aisle stock. The studio says the move reframes the brand as a working soap atelier, rather than a collection of ad-hoc labels.

stories.title: A typeface inspired by ink stains
stories.summary: Typeface maker DDOTT has released Pen, a font designed to mimic the ink pools that form when a pen nib pauses on paper. The letterforms are based on standardized industrial drafting scripts, with visual corrections applied to the stroke thickness. The font was created in collaboration with Morula.

stories.title: A calendar project born from creative burnout
stories.summary: Tajik designer Nigora Nasimova has created Shahnameh-2026, a calendar project that reimagines ancient Persian epic tales through modern graphic design. Nasimova says the project began during a period of creative burnout, drawing inspiration from a book on her shelf to bring historical cultural heritage into contemporary life.

stories.title: Ukraine introduces a national font to replace Russian designs
stories.summary: Ukraine has unveiled a new national typeface called Zakon, meaning law, to replace Russian-designed fonts like Izhitsa on official documents. The Ministry of Culture says the move follows years of requests from citizens and military personnel to stop using typefaces produced by the Russian foundry ParaType.

stories.title: USA Track and Field updates brand identity
stories.summary: USA Track and Field has launched a refreshed brand identity ahead of the LA 2028 Olympic Games. The federation says the new logo is intended to suggest a blend of the sport's heritage and its modern identity. It remains one of the largest sports in US high schools.

stories.title: Adobe asks teams to map out AI agent governance
stories.summary: Adobe has introduced Creative Agent assistants and local integrations that allow third-party agents to edit native project files. The company has not specified which brand rules take precedence when conflicts arise. Adobe suggests that teams map every agent route and name an owner before the private beta opens.

stories.title: Adobe previews experimental AI research tools
stories.summary: Adobe showcased ten research projects at its MAX Sneaks event, including a brush that understands image content. While these tools are experimental, the company notes that features from previous showcases often appear in software two years later. The tools aim to answer why creators still perform tasks by hand.

stories.title: Adobe expands AI agent integration across Creative Cloud
stories.summary: Adobe has announced a series of AI-powered upgrades for Firefly and Creative Cloud, focusing on natural language editing and task automation. The company says it wants to become a creative toolbox that does a little bit of everything. Partnerships with Google and Microsoft are also being strengthened.

stories.title: Adobe prepares for leadership transition
stories.summary: Adobe held its annual MAX conference in Miami Beach this week, the final event before Anil Chakravarthy succeeds Shantanu Narayen as CEO in December. The company is shifting its focus toward enterprise governance, model evaluations, and job-based pricing as it expands its AI partnerships with Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Adobe to enable native file editing for AI agents
stories.summary: Adobe plans to allow AI agents to edit native files starting in early 2027. The update is intended to integrate AI assistance directly into project workflows. Further details on the implementation of these agents are available for subscribers.

stories.title: Adobe announces new AI agents for enterprise workflows
stories.summary: Adobe has unveiled new AI agents and enterprise capabilities for its GenStudio and Creative Cloud platforms. The tools are designed to coordinate campaign planning and creative activation. The company says the updates aim to unify workflows across its various platforms while providing greater precision for third-party agents.

stories.title: Firefly transitions to an all-in-one creative platform
stories.summary: Adobe has repositioned its Firefly generative AI from a model family into a central creative platform. The company says the platform now helps users generate, edit, and produce content while maintaining consistency. New tools were introduced at Adobe MAX 2026 to support these connected, AI-powered workflows.

stories.title: Adobe updates Firefly and GenStudio workflows
stories.summary: Adobe has announced new AI agents and enterprise tools to unify workflows across Firefly, Creative Cloud, and GenStudio. The company says the updates include expanded design and prototyping tools. For enterprise users, a new CX Enterprise Coworker will coordinate campaign planning, creation, and activation across teams.

stories.title: Adobe expands the role of Firefly
stories.summary: Adobe has expanded Firefly from a generative AI model family into an all-in-one creative studio. The company says the platform is designed to help users maintain control and consistency while generating and editing content. New product platforms were introduced at Adobe MAX 2026 to support this evolution.

stories.title: Report finds office AI agents are becoming standard
stories.summary: A 2026 report on China's office intelligent agent market indicates that users are increasingly embedding AI into daily workflows. The study found that task delivery quality is now the primary factor in product competition, with desktop applications remaining the core scenario for initiating and executing office tasks.

stories.title: Disney and Adobe partner on AI storytelling
stories.summary: The Walt Disney Co. and Adobe have announced a multi-year partnership to integrate AI into Disney's storytelling and operations. Adobe will provide access to Firefly and other creative tools for use across Disney's resorts, cruise lines, and media divisions. Disney says it will focus on responsible AI innovation.

stories.title: Adobe promotes Firefly for content production
stories.summary: Adobe is positioning Firefly as an all-in-one creative workspace for generating images, videos, and audio. The company says the tool helps creators eliminate menial editing tasks and creative limitations. The platform is designed to help users produce professional-looking visuals to meet the demands of followers and brand partners.

stories.title: Testing the limits of AI app builders
stories.summary: Most AI app builders turn a paragraph of description into software within a single session. Differences emerge around the tenth prompt, when the cost of edits becomes clear and the responsibility for fixing broken code shifts. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Canva AI outputs are often predictable
stories.summary: Canva AI tools respond to instructions, but most Instagram posts made with the platform look the same. The company notes that generic results stem from short, vague prompts. A structured request produces a finished post, while a one-line request returns a template.

stories.title: Canva AI automates background removal
stories.summary: Canva uses AI to isolate subjects in photos, removing the need for manual tracing. The tool includes brushes for edge correction and supports bulk removal for up to 50 images per folder. It is intended for users who prefer to skip design experience.

stories.title: Bangalore interior studio shifts to certainty
stories.summary: Aishwarya Interiors says homeowners now prioritise certainty over style, wanting to know costs and decisions before manufacturing begins. The studio has delivered more than 5,000 homes since 2004. It now resolves design and cost together to address the demand for transparency.

stories.title: From Traditional Homes to Modern Spaces: Modular Interiors Transform India's Home Improvement Industry
stories.summary: India’s modular home interior market is emerging as a promising growth segment within the country’s expanding housing and consumer economy. Rapid urbanisation, rising residential demand, compact apartment layouts and changing household preferences are encouraging consumers to move beyond conventional carpentry towards factory-made modular furniture, customised

stories.title: Hamstech opens entrance test for design students
stories.summary: Hamstech College of Creative Education is inviting students to take the Hamstech Design Entrance Test. The previous iteration of the test saw 1,500 students participate, with 75 receiving scholarships. The exam aims to help young learners explore professional opportunities in the design industry.

stories.title: Vision Board Studio secures ISO certification
stories.summary: Mumbai-based Vision Board Studio has received ISO 9001:2015 certification for its quality management system. The firm specialises in visual merchandising and retail design for the jewellery and luxury sectors. The certification is intended to support the company as it eyes global expansion.

stories.title: Game design courses in India
stories.summary: India has become one of the world's largest gaming markets, with industry bodies estimating the sector could support 250,000 jobs. Studios are reportedly hiring faster than colleges can produce skilled workers. The challenge for those looking to enter the field remains choosing the right path among many options.

stories.title: Genesis patents GV90 design in India
stories.summary: Genesis has registered the design of its flagship GV90 electric SUV in India ahead of a planned 2027 brand launch. The vehicle features a 123.5 kWh battery and electric all-wheel-drive. It is positioned to compete in the upper end of the global luxury SUV market.

stories.title: Inc42 and DevX launch proptech investment pool
stories.summary: India's real estate industry is estimated at $650 billion, yet the sector remains dependent on traditional, manual processes. Inc42 and DevX have launched a 15 crore rupee investment pool to support startups attempting to bring technological transformation to the market. Building real estate technology comes with unique challenges.

stories.title: Zelio E-Mobility profit grows
stories.summary: Zelio E-Mobility reported a 164.3 percent increase in net profit to 31.4 crore rupees for the first half of fiscal year 2027. Operating revenue grew 120 percent to 296.7 crore rupees. Total expenses for the period more than doubled to 261.5 crore rupees.

stories.title: Wakefit profit remains flat
stories.summary: Wakefit reported a net profit of 15.9 crore rupees for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, flat compared to the year-ago period. The company attributed a 32 percent sequential profit decline to rising commodity prices and geopolitical disruptions. The operating environment remains challenging for the mattress brand.

stories.title: Zaggle profit declines
stories.summary: Zaggle reported a 30 percent year-over-year profit decline to 24.5 crore rupees for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. Operating revenue grew 34.2 percent, and the company noted its SaaS business recorded its highest-ever quarterly performance. Total expenses surged 39.9 percent during the same period.

stories.title: Zetwerk reports wider quarterly loss
stories.summary: Zetwerk reported a 43.2 percent year-over-year increase in net loss to 88.1 crore rupees for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. Operating revenue grew 18.3 percent to 4,599.4 crore rupees. The company recorded net exceptional gains of 1.3 crore rupees from continuing operations.

stories.title: Yatra reports quarterly loss
stories.summary: Yatra reported a consolidated net loss of 78.4 lakh rupees for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to a profit of 14.3 crore rupees in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations fell 39.1 percent to 213.6 crore rupees. The company cited a challenging operating environment.

stories.title: Adobe Max conference in Miami
stories.summary: Adobe is hosting its annual conference to reveal upcoming AI-based tools for Photoshop and Premiere. The event focuses on the future of creative products and software updates. The conference name remains a coincidence.

stories.title: Drogue plans floating data centers
stories.summary: Startup Drogue is developing a system to harvest ocean heat to power floating data centers. CEO Sam Sipe claims the technology will help developers deploy servers in AI-friendly timelines. The company expects a prototype to be operational within two years. The data center industry is a real estate game.

stories.title: Drogue raises 20 million dollars
stories.summary: Drogue has raised 20 million dollars to build floating data centers powered by ocean temperature gradients. The company plans to deploy a multi-megawatt prototype on a converted ship by early 2028. The design has received approval in principle from the American Bureau of Shipping.

stories.title: AI industry faces market uncertainty
stories.summary: Following recent ballot measures and a spy scandal involving Nvidia, the AI industry is experiencing a period of volatility. Speculation regarding the stability of the AI bubble has increased alongside a drop in share prices. The industry was previously described as unstoppable.

stories.title: AI impact on Indian outsourcing
stories.summary: AI is automating repetitive tasks like rotoscoping and project management for small Indian creative agencies. By separating capability from headcount, the technology allows smaller teams to compete for global work. This shift could potentially reshape the country's export model.

stories.title: Canva announces job cuts
stories.summary: Canva will cut or relocate up to 1,200 roles following a year of slowed growth. CEO Melanie Perkins stated the firm needs to be refound, while insisting that human tasks will not be replaced by artificial intelligence. The union representing employees has commented on the restructure.

stories.title: Nvidia begins search for new CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia has begun a search for a permanent CEO following the resignation of Jensen Huang after 33 years. The board is considering internal and external candidates, while CFO Colette Kress serves as interim lead. The leadership transition follows a week of market instability for the chipmaker.

stories.title: Arena Broadcast hiring scheduler
stories.summary: Arena Broadcast is seeking a junior programme scheduler to manage content for The Home Channel and IGNITION TV. The role requires an individual to maintain daily and weekly television schedules. The position is based in Parktown, Johannesburg.

stories.title: Librarian retires after 30 years at Western Michigan University
stories.summary: Randle Gedeon will retire from Western Michigan University this December after 30 years of service. Gedeon, who holds master degrees in Education and Library Science, previously worked at John Carroll University and Northeastern State University. He notes that libraries are a good place to spend time at work.

stories.title: Graphic design software shifts as Canva and Adobe diverge
stories.summary: Canva recently relaunched Affinity as a free app for vector, photo and layout tools, now available on iPad. Adobe has focused its recent efforts on generative and agent-based AI tools for Photoshop and Illustrator. Choosing software is no longer as simple as it used to be.
